{{Otheruses|Seeker}}
[[File:Alien2_-_GG11.png|thumb|right|200px|A seeker droid immobilizes a target.]]
A '''seeker''' was a specialized type of [[Remote/Legends|remote]] that was programmed to track down a specific target with the intention of either capturing or killing them.

==Description==
Seekers were small, spherical devices that were visually similar to [[Remote/Legends|remotes]].<ref name="NEGWT">''[[The New Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref>

==History==
Seekers were developed by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], and were originally designed to be non-lethal. Their mission parameters included tracking down specific targets, being used for investigations, and even as emergency [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguards]].<ref name="EGWT">''[[The Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref>

When the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] rose to power, seekers were given increased autonomy, and were armed with lethal weapons so that they could kill their assigned target if necessary. These seekers were often tasked with kill orders, and were deployed against individuals that Imperial [[Officer/Legends|officers]] considered to be "enemies of the state." These included political opponents, known [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance]] [[operative]]s, and even rival officers.<ref name="EGWT" /> Imperial search droids could be dispatched to hunt down or find a specific personage.  They were used by [[Haninum Tyk Rhinann]] during his hunt for [[Jax Pavan]].<ref name="Coruscant">''[[Coruscant Nights I: Jedi Twilight]]''</ref>

The [[Fromm Gang/Legends|Fromm Gang]] used seekers to guard their territory,<ref name="WW">{{DroidsCite|The White Witch}}</ref> as well as [[Mine/Legends|mines]].<ref name="Escape">[[Star Wars: Droids (video game)|''Star Wars: Droids'' video game]]</ref>

Lethal seekers were banned once the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] took control of the galactic government. Although seekers were still used, they were heavily restricted, used by [[Law enforcement agency/Legends|law enforcement agencies]] for surveillance and security purposes. These units were armed only with [[Stun blaster/Legends|stun blasters]].<ref name="EGWT" />

==Behind the scenes==
Search droids were included in the revised rough draft of the [[1999]] [[prequel trilogy]] film {{Film|I}}. In the draft, the droids were affiliated with the [[Trade Federation Droid Army/Legends|Trade Federation Droid Army]], and were dispatched to track down the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] by [[22D-R]] on the orders of the [[B1-series battle droid|B1 battle droid]] [[OOM-9/Legends|OOM-9]]. One of the droids followed Kenobi to the [[Water/Legends|underwater]] [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] [[City/Legends|city]] [[Otoh Gunga/Legends|Otoh Gunga]], where it was destroyed by Kenobi. The 1999 CD-ROM ''[[Star Wars: Episode I Insider's Guide]]'' mentioned their role in the screenplay, and referred to the droids additionally as "remote seekers."<ref name="Insiders">[[Star Wars: Episode I Insider's Guide|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Insider's Guide'']]</ref>
